beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does everyone want Greenland?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It's the largest island on Earth. About fifty-six thousand people live there, and most of it is under ice.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where is it, exactly?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Between North America and Europe. Geographically it's North American, but it belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who got there first?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Arctic peoples came first. Then, around 985, Erik the Red brought Norse settlers from Iceland.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The sagas say he called it Greenland to attract settlers. The Norse farmed the south-west for four centuries.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Then they vanished. The last record is a wedding at Hvalsey Church in 1408. The Inuit stayed.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So how did Denmark get it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1721, the missionary Hans Egede arrived from Denmark-Norway, and Danish rule followed.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does America care?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The map. Greenland, Iceland and Britain frame the GIUK gap, the sea gate between the Arctic and the Atlantic.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In the Cold War, Soviet submarines from Murmansk had to slip through it.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1946, Truman secretly offered a hundred million dollars in gold. Denmark said no, so America built Thule Air Base.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Today it's Pituffik Space Base, watching for missiles over the Pole.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Is Greenland still a colony?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Not any more. Home rule came in 1979, self-government in 2009, with the right to choose independence.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So why all the headlines?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: As the ice melts, sea routes and minerals open up. In 2025, Donald Trump said America needed Greenland and would not rule out force.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In September 2026, the three governments signed a deal: more American bases, and Greenland stays in the Danish realm.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: the Taiwan Strait. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
